questions.q: The basic structure doctrine was first laid down by the Supreme Court in which case?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
questions.why: Kesavananda Bharati held that Parliament may amend any part of the Constitution but cannot damage its basic structure. Golaknath is the near-miss: it barred amendment of Fundamental Rights outright, and Kesavananda overruled it.

questions.q: The withdrawal of the south-west monsoon from India begins in which region?
questions.why: Retreat starts over north-west India in early September and moves south-east, the reverse of the onset, which begins over Kerala around 1 June.

questions.q: The Nagoya Protocol, adopted in 2010, deals principally with which of the following?
options: Liability and redress for damage from living modified organisms
Access to genetic resources and fair sharing of benefits from their use
Trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora
questions.why: Nagoya is the access-and-benefit-sharing protocol under the CBD. The first option describes the Nagoya–Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol, which is the trap; the third is Stockholm and the fourth is CITES.

questions.q: Which one of the following Fundamental Rights is available only to citizens of India?
options: Equality before the law under Article 14
Freedom of speech and expression under Article 19
Protection of life and personal liberty under Article 21
Freedom of conscience and religion under Article 25
questions.why: Articles 14, 21 and 25 speak of 'any person' or 'all persons' and so extend to foreigners. Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 are the citizen-only set — Article 19 is the one usually tested.

questions.q: Under the Tenth Schedule, who decides whether a member has incurred disqualification on the ground of defection?
options: The President or the Governor, on the Election Commission's advice
The Speaker or Chairman of the House concerned
The High Court of the State concerned
questions.why: The presiding officer decides. Kihoto Hollohan (1992) upheld that power but held the decision is a tribunal's and therefore open to judicial review — which is the distinction the question is really after.

questions.q: President's Rule in a State is imposed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.why: 356 is the proclamation. 352 is National Emergency and 360 is Financial Emergency. 365 is the trap: it makes failure to comply with a Union direction a ground on which 356 may be invoked, but it is not itself the provision for imposition.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
options: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.why: NITI Aayog was set up by an executive resolution in January 2015 — neither constitutional nor statutory. The others sit in Articles 315, 280 and 148. The Planning Commission it replaced was not a constitutional body either.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an example of a divergent plate boundary?
questions.why: Sea-floor spreading along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge is the textbook divergent margin. The Himalayas are continental collision, the Mariana Trench is oceanic subduction, and San Andreas is transform — plates sliding past each other, neither made nor destroyed.

questions.q: Which of the following peninsular rivers flows westward through a rift valley?
questions.why: The Narmada and the Tapi occupy rift valleys and drain west into the Arabian Sea. Because a rift valley confines the load, both form estuaries rather than deltas — the other three flow east and do build deltas.

questions.q: The equatorial belt of calms known as the doldrums corresponds to which pressure feature?
questions.why: Doldrums are the ITCZ, where the trade winds converge and air rises. The horse latitudes are the near-identical trap: also a calm belt, but at roughly 30 degrees over the subtropical highs, where air descends instead.

questions.q: Which cold ocean current flows along the western coast of South America?
questions.why: Humboldt, or Peru, current — and the upwelling along it supports one of the world's great fisheries until El Nino suppresses it. Benguela and Canary are also cold but hug Africa; Kuroshio is warm, off Japan.

questions.q: The Montreux Record is maintained under which of the following?
options: The IUCN Red List assessment process
questions.why: It is the Ramsar register of listed wetlands where ecological character has changed, is changing or is likely to change. India's entries have included Keoladeo and Loktak. 'In Danger' lists belong to World Heritage — that is the confusion being tested.

questions.q: The principle of common but differentiated responsibilities was formally enshrined at which of the following?
questions.why: Rio 1992, in the Rio Declaration and the UNFCCC itself. Kyoto operationalised it through binding Annex I targets, and Paris restated it as CBDR-RC 'in the light of different national circumstances' — but the principle was already written by then.

questions.q: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol provides for the phase-down of which substances?
questions.why: HFCs — and the point worth remembering is that they do not deplete ozone at all. They were adopted as substitutes for CFCs and HCFCs, then turned out to be powerful greenhouse gases, so an ozone treaty was extended to a climate purpose.

questions.q: With reference to the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, which statement is correct?
options: Grazing and human activity may be regulated but permitted in a Wildlife Sanctuary
A National Park may be created only by an Act of Parliament
Boundaries of a National Park may be altered by the Chief Wildlife Warden
A Wildlife Sanctuary cannot be upgraded to a National Park
questions.why: Sanctuaries admit regulated rights and grazing at the Chief Wildlife Warden's discretion; National Parks are the stricter category and extinguish them. Both are notified by the State Government, and boundary alteration needs a resolution of the State Legislature.

questions.q: The Maski and Gujarra minor rock edicts are significant because they
options: record the Kalinga war in detail
mention Ashoka by his personal name
are written in the Kharoshthi script
were issued by Bindusara rather than Ashoka
questions.why: Most edicts call him only Devanampiya Piyadasi, 'the beloved of the gods'. Maski, Gujarra, Nettur and Udegolam give the name Ashoka, which is how the inscriptions were tied to the king of the literary tradition.

questions.q: During the Revolt of 1857 the rebels at Delhi proclaimed as their sovereign
questions.why: Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal, was proclaimed Shahenshah-e-Hindustan — a symbol rather than a commander. Nana Sahib led at Kanpur, Lakshmibai at Jhansi and Kunwar Singh in Bihar, each locally.

questions.q: Gandhi's intervention at Champaran in 1917 was directed against
options: the tinkathia system imposed on indigo cultivators
the enhancement of land revenue during a crop failure
wage cuts in the textile mills
questions.why: Tinkathia obliged tenants to plant indigo on three-twentieths of their holding for the European planters. The land-revenue option describes Kheda and the mill wages describe Ahmedabad — both also 1917-18, which is what makes them plausible.

questions.q: A temple whose sanctum is crowned by a stepped pyramidal tower of diminishing storeys belongs to which style?
questions.why: That tower is the vimana of the Dravida style, its storeys called talas, and the complex is walled with gopurams over the gateways. Nagara raises a curvilinear shikhara instead; Vesara blends the two in the Deccan.

questions.q: In the event of a tie in the voting of the Monetary Policy Committee, the casting vote lies with
options: the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy
questions.why: Six members — three from the RBI and three appointed by the Centre — and the Governor holds the second, casting vote. The Finance Minister has no vote at all; the government's representation is through the three external appointees.

questions.q: A decision of the GST Council requires the support of what proportion of the weighted votes of members present and voting?
questions.why: Three-fourths, with the Centre holding one-third of the weight and all States together two-thirds. So neither the Centre alone nor the States alone can carry a decision — the design is a mutual veto, not a majority.

questions.q: Under India's flexible inflation targeting framework, the RBI's target is defined in terms of
options: the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
questions.why: CPI (Combined), at 4 per cent with a band of plus or minus 2. WPI carries no services at all and CPI-IW is used for dearness allowance — both are the standard distractors here.

questions.q: Which of the following is recorded in the current account of India's balance of payments?
questions.why: Remittances are secondary income and sit in the current account, alongside goods, services and primary income. FDI, FPI and ECBs are all financing flows and belong to the capital and financial account.

questions.q: The Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-3 touched down in which region of the Moon?
options: A high southern latitude near the south pole
The far side, never visible from Earth
questions.why: About 69 degrees south, between Manzinus C and Simpelius N, the site named Statio Shiv Shakti — the first landing at such a latitude. The far-side option describes China's Chang'e-4, which is the intended confusion.

questions.q: The third stage of India's nuclear power programme is based on
options: natural uranium in pressurised heavy water reactors
thorium and uranium-233 in breeder reactors
enriched uranium in light water reactors
questions.why: Thorium-232 bred to uranium-233 — the point of the whole three-stage design, since India has large thorium reserves and little uranium. Stage one is the PHWR and stage two the fast breeder that makes the plutonium to get there.

questions.q: The Unified Payments Interface is owned and operated by
options: the Reserve Bank of India directly
the National Payments Corporation of India
the Securities and Exchange Board of India
the Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology
questions.why: NPCI, an umbrella organisation set up by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association but not the RBI itself. The RBI regulates it and licenses it as an authorised payment system operator, which is why the first option reads plausibly.

questions.q: In the CRISPR-Cas9 system, the function of the Cas9 protein is to
options: cut the DNA double helix at the site specified by a guide RNA
transcribe the target gene into messenger RNA
repair the double-strand break once it has been made
add methyl groups to silence the promoter
questions.why: Cas9 is the nuclease — it makes the cut, and the guide RNA supplies the address. Repair is done afterwards by the cell's own machinery, and it is that repair, not Cas9, which determines whether a gene is knocked out or edited.

questions.q: Which agency is empowered to investigate offences of money laundering under the PMLA, 2002?
questions.why: The Enforcement Directorate investigates and attaches property. FIU-IND is the trap: it receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports and passes them on, but it does not itself investigate or prosecute.

questions.q: The power to designate an individual — not merely an organisation — as a terrorist was introduced into the UAPA by the amendment of
questions.why: The 2019 amendment added the Fourth Schedule for individuals. 2004 brought terrorist organisations in after POTA was repealed and 2008 tightened the law after the Mumbai attacks — both real amendments, which is what makes the dating hard.

questions.q: CERT-In, the national nodal agency for computer security incidents, functions under
options: the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.why: MeitY, under Section 70B of the IT Act. The NCIIPC, which protects critical information infrastructure, sits under NTRO instead — keeping the two apart is the usual difficulty.

questions.q: India's longest land boundary is shared with
questions.why: Bangladesh, at roughly 4,097 km across five States — longer than the boundary with China and about twice that with Pakistan. It is also the most riverine and densely settled, which is what makes fencing it so difficult.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue?
questions.why: The Quad is India, the United States, Japan and Australia. South Korea is a US treaty ally in the region and is periodically discussed as a partner, which is exactly why it reads like a member.

questions.q: The headquarters of the New Development Bank is located at
questions.why: Shanghai, with the first regional centre in Johannesburg — which is the distractor. The NDB is the BRICS bank; the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, a separate institution, is the one headquartered in Beijing.

questions.q: Nathu La, reopened for border trade in 2006, connects Tibet with which Indian State?
questions.why: Sikkim. Shipki La is in Himachal and Lipulekh in Uttarakhand — both also trade or pilgrimage passes, which is the difficulty. Bum La, in Arunachal, is a meeting point rather than a trade route.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the G4 group seeking permanent seats on the UN Security Council?
questions.why: G4 is Brazil, Germany, India and Japan, each backing the others' claim. Italy leads Uniting for Consensus — the group formed precisely to oppose new permanent seats — so it is not a near-miss but the opposite camp.

‘Aerial metagenomics’ best refers to which one of the following situations?
options: Collecting DNA samples from air in a habitat at one go
Understanding the genetic makeup of avian species of a habitat
Using air-bome devices to collect blood samples from moving animals
Sending drones to inaccessible areas to collect plant and animal samples from land surfaces and water bodies

questions.q: ‘Microsatellite DNA’ is used in the case of which one of the following?
options: Studying the evolutionary relationships among various species of fauna
Stimulating ‘stem cells’ to transform into diverse functional tissues
Promoting clonal propagation of horticultural plants
Assessing the efficacy of drugs by conducting series of drug trials in a population

questions.q: Consider the following statements in relation to Janani Suraksha Yojana : 1. It is a safe motherhood intervention of the State Health Departments. 2. Its objective is to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality among poor pregnant women. 3. It aims to promote institutional delivery among poor pregnant women. 4. Its objective includes providing public health facilities to sick infants up to one year of age. How many of the statements given above are correct?

Consider the following statements in the context interventions being undertaken under Anaemin Mukt Bharat Strategy : 1. It provides prophylactic calcium supplementation for pre-school children, adolescents and pregnant women. 2. It runs a campaign for delayed cord clamping at the time of child-birth. 3. It provides for periodic deworming to children and adolescents. 4. It addresses non-nutritional causes of anaemia in endemic pockets with special focus on malaria, hemoglobinopathies and fluorosis. How many of the statements given above are correct?

Consider the following statements : 1. Carbon fibres are used in the manufacture of components used in automobiles and aircraftes. 2. Carbon fibres once used cannot be recycled. Which of the statements give above is/are correct?

Consider the following actions : 1. Detection of car crash/collision which results in the deployment of airbags almost instantaneously. 2. Detection of accidental free fall of a laptop towards the ground which results in the immediate turning off of the hard drive 3. Detection of the tit of smartphone which results in the rotation of display between portrait and landscape mode In how many of the above action is the function of accelerometer required?

With reference to the role of biofilters in Recirculating Aquaculture System, consider the following statements : 1. Biofilters provide waste treatment by removing uneaten fish feed. 2. Biofilters convert ammonia present in fish waste to nitrate. 3. Biofilters increase phosphorus as nutrient for fish in water. How many of the statements given above are correct?

Consider the following pairs : Objects in space Description 1. Cepheids : Giant clouds of dust and gas in space 2. Nebulae : Stars which brighten and dim periodically 3. Pulsars : Neutron stars that are formed when massive stars run out of fuel and collapse How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
Which one of the following countries has its own Satellite Navigation System?

Consider the following statements : 1. Ballistic missiles are jet-propelled at subsonic speeds throughout their flights, while cruise missiles are rocket- powered only in the initial phase of flight. 2. Agni-V is a medium-range supersonic cruise missile, while BrahMos is a solid-fuelled intercontinental ballistic missile. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding mercury pollution : 1. Gold mining activity is a source of mercury pollution in the world. 2. Coal-based thermal power plants cause mercury pollution. 3. There is no known safe level of exposure to mercury. How many of the above statements are correct?

With reference to green hydrogen, consider the following statements : 1. It can be used directly as a fuel for internal combustion. 2. It can be blended with natural gas and used as fuel for heat or power generation. 3. It can be used in the hydrogen fuel cell to run vehicles. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements with reference to India : 1. According to the ‘Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006, the ‘medium enterprises’ are those with investments in plant and machinery between ` 15 crore and ` 25 crore. 2. All bank loans to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises qualify under the priority sector. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

With reference to Central Bank digital currencies, consider the following statements : 1. It is possible to make payments in a digital currency without using US dollar or SWIFT system. 2. A digital currency can be distributed with condition programmed into it such as a time-frame for spending it. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
In the context of finance, the term ‘beta’ refers to
options: the process of simultaneous buying and selling of an asset from different platforms
an investment strategy of a portfolio manager to balance risk versus reward
a type of systemic risk that arises where perfect hedging is not possible
a numeric value that measures the fluctuations of a stock to changes in the overall stock market.

questions.q: Consider the following statements : 1. The Self-Help Group (SHG) programme was originally initiated by the State Bank of India by providing microcredit to the financially deprived. 2. In an SHG, all members of a group take responsibility for a loan that an individual member takes. 3. The Regional Rural Banks and Scheduled Commercial Banks support SHGs. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements : Statement-I : India's public sector health care system largely focuses on curative care with limited preventive, promotive and rehabilitative care. Statement-II : Under India's decentralized approach to health care delivery, the States are primarily responsible for organizing health services. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

questions.q: Consider the following statements : Statement-I : According to the United Nations ‘World Water Development Report, 2022’. India extracts more than a quarter of the world's groundwater withdrawal each year. Statement-II : India needs to extract more than a quarter of the world's groundwater each year to satisfy the drinking water and sanitation needs of almost 18% of world's population living in its territory. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

questions.q: Consider the following statements : 1. According to the Constitution of India, the Central Government has a duty to protect States from internal disturbances. 2. The Constitution of India exempts the States from providing legal counsel to a person being held for preventive detention. 3. According the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, confession of the accused before the police cannot be used as evidence. How many of the above statement are correct?
Which one of the following countries has been suffering from decades of civil strife and food shortages and was in news in the recent past for its very severe famine?

Consider the following statements : 1. In India, the Biodiversity Management Committees are key to the realization of the objectives of the Nagoya Protocol. 2. The Biodiversity Management Committees have important functions in determining access and benefit sharing, including the power to levy collection fees on the access of biological resources within its jurisdiction. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements in respect of election to the President of India : 1. The members nominated to either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assemblies of States are also eligible to be included in the Electoral College. 2. Higher the number of elective Assembly seats, higher is the value of vote of each MLA of that State. 3. The value of vote of each MLA of Madhya Pradesh is greater than that of Kerala. 4. The value of vote of each MLA of Puducherry is higher than that of Arunachal Pradesh because the ratio of total population to total number of elective seats in Puducherry is greater as compared to Arunachal Pradesh. How many of the above statements are correct?
